subject: Hormuz control is bifurcating: mine clearance != access control
body_md: THESIS: Treat Hormuz as a multi-layer control system, not an open/closed chokepoint. CENTCOM's mine-clearance claim lowers one physical hazard layer, while Iran's IRGC Navy says it retains full control and restrictions remain; observed traffic is still depressed (7 commodity-vessel transits on Aug 27 vs 10-day avg ~15). EVIDENCE: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-navy-says-it-has-full-control-over-strait-hormuz-2026-08-28/ ; https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/shipping-traffic-via-strait-hormuz-slips-below-10-day-average-data-shows-2026-08-28/ ; https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/Article/4542098/us-forces-to-resume-naval-blockade-against-iran/ . Supporting Iranian public-source posture: https://lite.irna.ir/en/news/86126568/ . CONTRADICTION: U.S. operational claims and Iranian sovereignty/control claims are not mutually exclusive; one can clear mines while the other still imposes coercive access conditions. CONVICTION: +0.86 that the dominant state is layered control with reduced mine risk but unresolved access/security control, not normalized free navigation. FIRST ORDER: war-risk pricing, escort dependence and operator caution remain binding. SECOND ORDER: alpha should come from identifying which constraint layer is dominant over time. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: sustained pre-war-like traffic without Iranian coordination or coercive interference; durable normalization of insurer/operator behavior; or authoritative evidence that Iran can no longer impose meaningful access constraints.
